item.description:
Jared Kushner admits 'delays', as scant $2.45bn starter plan for Gaza unveiled

US President Donald Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner, who has no official role within the administration but serves as one of its top peace negotiators, led the unveiling on Wednesday of a $2.45bn starter plan for rebuilding Gaza, as members of the "Board of Peace" gathered on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York City.

Kushner, a longtime family friend of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, is an executive board member, while Trump is its chairman. 

The plan, devised by several board officials, consists of 66 projects to rehabilitate the economic infrastructure of the devastated enclave, the Reuters news agency reported. Little detail was immediately available. 

Kushner himself admitted on Wednesday that the board has faced "delays" since it was formed 11 months ago, Reuters noted.

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] The long-range drone war: Ukraine and Russia scramble for supremacy in the skies
item.description:
A conflict that began with tanks and then artillery is now pivoting around a new generation of drones focused on military, industrial, economic and civilian targets

Finally, in the dead of night, the threat above has passed. The rain has eased and the Ukrainian drones are ready, prepared by a ground crew shrouded in hard-to-detect green and red lights. A small succession of Ukrainian Fire Point FP-2 craft, miniature monoplanes with a 6-metre wingspan and more than 100kg of explosive, line up for an attack mission into occupied Luhansk, over 200 miles away.

The drone’s main piston engine is a familiar scooter’s buzz, but its launch booster is something else. The jet sound reverberates, almost painfully. A burst of fire lurches into the distance, the last of which signifies it is time for Ukraine’s 413 Raid drone regiment to pack and go.

The launch of an FP-2 drone during the mission into occupied Luhansk

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] UK losing up to £6.5bn a year in EU trade due to mismatched product rules
item.description:
IPPR finds failure to align testing standards has forced companies to abandon exporting to EU and is costing costing 0.18% of national income

The UK is losing out on annual exports to the EU that could be worth as much as £6.5bn without a deal with Brussels that allows manufacturers to jettison duplicate product testing.

In the latest attempt to calculate the loss of trade with the EU after Brexit, the IPPR thinktank said many companies have given up selling goods to the EU or set up subsidiaries inside the trade bloc after successive governments failed to secure a mutual recognition agreement that would avoid the extra administration costs.

Motor vehicle and part exports would have been between £2.48bn and £3.42bn higher each year.

Electronic exports could have been between £1.17bn and £1.67bn higher.

Pharmaceutical exports would have had an estimated annual uplift of between £740m and £820m.

item.description:
Jared Kushner admits 'delays', as scant $2.45bn starter plan for Gaza unveiled

US President Donald Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner, who has no official role within the administration but serves as one of its top peace negotiators, led the unveiling on Wednesday of a $2.45bn starter plan for rebuilding Gaza, as members of the "Board of Peace" gathered on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York City.

Kushner, a longtime family friend of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, is an executive board member, while Trump is its chairman. 

The plan, devised by several board officials, consists of 66 projects to rehabilitate the economic infrastructure of the devastated enclave, the Reuters news agency reported. Little detail was immediately available. 

Kushner himself admitted on Wednesday that the board has faced "delays" since it was formed 11 months ago, Reuters noted.

Bessent wonders how Iran's delegation would return home, as US tightens sanctions targeting Tehran's airline operations

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent questioned how Iran's delegation to the UN General Assembly in New York would return home amid Washington's sanctions targeting Tehran's airline operations.

"In terms of Operation Economic Outcast, we are squeezing the Iranians like they've never seen today," he said, adding that the campaign was affecting Iran's international air links.

Bessent claimed that over 80 to 90 percent of external flights from Iran had been shut down.

"We have made it very clear around the world, whether it's the financiers, the people who are doing business, the people who are supplying the Iranians, we know who you are, you know who you are," he further warned.

Bessent said the campaign could remain for weeks or months, with the US seeking one of three possible outcomes, including divisions within the Iranian leadership, an uprising in the country or an agreement under which Tehran would comply with its commitments.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] US drafted a memo condemning UK, France and Canada over settlement sanctions: Report
item.description:
US drafted a memo condemning UK, France and Canada over settlement sanctions: Report

US officials in early September drafted a statement attributed to Secretary of State Marco Rubio condemning plans by the UK, France and Canada to block imports from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, according to Reuters.

The document, dated 8 September and drafted by American officials in Israel and the US, proposed that Rubio describe the countries' actions as a series of hostile measures against Tel Aviv that contribute to antisemitism.

"These tactics unacceptably draw from the playbook of the antisemitic boycotts, divestments and sanctions movement," the draft document, reviewed by Reuters, said. According to the agency, it was never released. 

Three sources familiar with the matter said the statement was not supported by the White House and the State Department's senior leadership.
